decisions.rationale: Verified on a git archive of 0e12a9f7 with the private completed work applied: giving the tags an inline-block display, or a table display, while keeping their correct own widths fails only task 11, on the fill-the-checklist control, whose message names a wrapper, float, columns or positioning around the tag; a flow-root display passes all 12. The narrowing is fair and README task 11 does ask for ordinary blocks, but README Troubleshooting says the failure means the 200px is coming from something around the tag, which is false when the tag's own display makes it shrink to its text, and the solved-run variantRuns sentence repeats that attribution for the inline-block variant. Nothing learner-facing defines an ordinary block, and inline-block chips are the most likely way a learner meets this control. Smallest correct fix: in the control's failure message and in the Troubleshooting sentence, name the tag's own display (inline-block or table-style) or a float on the tag as a cause alongside its surroundings and say the tag must keep the default block display, then correct the variantRuns attribution when the solved run is re-recorded. This change, like every accepted finding here, would be a further correction loop, which workflow 2.4 escalates; that escalation is handled separately.

Verified at 8e3154b6: the record's 'contract' field says the run was exercised on a fresh pep export-lab bundle, while its first procedure step says the lab was taken with git archive into a private directory; 'privateStaging' says the solution existed only in a private temporary copy of the export during the run, while 'cleanup' says the completed files stay in uncommitted private staging. The record contradicts itself on how the run was made and what remains. environment.os still reads Darwin 25.6.0, while the host that made this recent run reports Darwin 27.2.0 with the same recorded Node and npm versions, so the OS line is very likely stale. The core claims hold: all thirteen artifactHashes match the 0e12a9f7 bytes, the starter fails 12 of 12 and the completed work passes 12 of 12 in my own runs. Smallest correct fix: rewrite 'contract' and 'privateStaging' to describe the git-archive run and the retained private staging, and re-record environment.os from the host that ran it, leaving hashes and results unchanged. Same fix as cl3-sme-004.

The Tasks preamble sentence is explicitly scoped to the TODO task comments in the sign-up corner of index.html and is true as written; the task 11 TODO comment in the gear checklist states its own purpose (style the tags in styles.css and keep their classes), and README task 11's Where line already names both files and says the tags are already in the gear checklist, so no learner is misdirected. On the border style, I reproduced that a dashed border passes, but README 'What the tests check' says task 11 measures the padding and border sizes, not their style, and the lab elsewhere states outcomes the tests do not fully measure and lists hand checks separately; a stated requirement that is stricter than the test is not a false claim and costs the learner nothing. No correction is warranted.

The finding itself confirms the timing is honest: lab.json minutes and notes and README line 3 agree on a 53-minute median and 60-minute cap, both labelled an unmeasured authoring estimate, the task-by-task breakdown sums to the median, and the cap stays inside the 62 minutes of S21 Guided lab; the same critic's recheck item edu-t1 marks the timing resolved on these bytes, and lab-contract.md sets no buffer size. Most of the README growth is the task 11 section, its test description and its Troubleshooting line, which a learner reads while doing task 11 rather than in the up-front read. A tighter buffer is a planning risk, not a defect; the right evidence to revisit it is a measured pilot, not a wording change now. No correction is warranted.

Reproduced on a git archive of 0e12a9f7: the private completed work plus only a transition on all properties of the gear checklist fails task 11 (11 pass, 1 fail), with the fill-the-checklist message reporting the tag still at the first pinned checklist width when the second is in force, and wrongly telling the learner to remove a wrapper, float, columns or positioning. The pinned() map sets many properties inline with importance but not transition or animation, and transition declarations outrank important author declarations in the cascade, so a harmless polish rule produces a false fail with a misleading message. Low, because the lab never asks for a transition, but real. Smallest correct fix: add transition and animation neutralisation to the pinned() map for the checklist and set the same on each tag, restoring afterwards, before any measurement.

Verified by reading the test at 0e12a9f7: the two box-sizing assertions read only runs[0] (the first window and checklist width), while every other per-tag check runs in all four cases, and README 'What the tests check' and lab.json notes list box-sizing among the measured items without that restriction, so a stylesheet that switches a tag's sizing model only at the wider window is not caught. The content-box calculation is still forced in the first case, so the objective is still practised, which keeps this low. Smallest correct fix: move the two box-sizing assertions inside the existing loop over runs so each case checks both tags' models.

Reproduced on a git archive of 0e12a9f7: the private completed work with the tags relatively positioned and offset sideways passes all 12 tests, yet README 'What the tests check' says task 11 rejects moving a tag; the test rejects only the transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom properties, which lab.json notes state accurately. The broader Outcome wording about ordinary blocks directly in the checklist is a requirement stricter than the test, which is harmless, and none of these variants lets the stated size skip the calculation. Smallest correct fix: change 'moving' to 'translating' in that README line so it matches lab.json, and, together with the cl3-edu-001 fix, word Troubleshooting as the tag failing to fill the checklist rather than implying every wrapper or positioning fails.

Same verified defect as cl3-edu-002: the 'contract' and 'privateStaging' fields, carried over from the earlier record, contradict the record's own procedure (git archive, not pep export-lab) and cleanup (private copy retained in uncommitted staging), and environment.os (Darwin 25.6.0) does not match the Darwin 27.2.0 host whose Node and npm versions the record reports. The hashes and results verify on current bytes. Medium is the fitting grade: the record is evidence the gate relies on and must describe the run truthfully. Smallest correct fix: rewrite those two fields to describe the git-archive run and retained private staging and re-record environment.os from the running host, leaving hashes and results unchanged.

Verified by reading the test at 0e12a9f7: both runs call setViewportSize with a different width but the same height, so any length in height-based viewport units resolves identically in all four cases, and the control is unaffected because it removes the tag's own width; a tag sized that way passes although it is not the stated size in a browser window of another height. README Troubleshooting says a width that depends on the window fails when the test changes those sizes, which is false for these units. This reopens part of an earlier window-dependence concern, so medium is fitting. Smallest correct fix: give the two runs different window heights as well as widths, paired so that width-based, height-based, smaller-side and larger-side viewport units all change between runs, and add a height-based-unit variant to the solved-run matrix.
